subject.title: ci: harden HTTP and local-auth gates against transient failures

question: Should the HTTP live-fixture hardening land independently while local-auth capacity, query-load, and retry behavior are handled as a separately owned CI track?
rationale: The HTTP fix is narrow, but local-auth work crosses runner-provider capacity, workflow cost, browser retry design, frontend subscription load, and diagnostic policy; maintainers must choose ownership and sequencing.

options.title: Split and sequence
options.body: Land a focused HTTP fixture or retry fix first, then scope local-auth diagnostics and load reduction under a separately owned follow-up with explicit runner-cost approval.

options.title: Keep one coordinated issue
options.body: Retain this issue as the umbrella and require coordinated workflow, frontend-query, and Playwright changes with one shared repetition plan.

recommendation.title: Split and sequence
recommendation.body: Land a focused HTTP fixture or retry fix first, then scope local-auth diagnostics and load reduction under a separately owned follow-up with explicit runner-cost approval.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent merged work provides the strongest current ownership signal across the CI workflow and local-auth runner configuration.
